transcript.content: Hello, I am Dr. Smith. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi. Um... I guess I'm here because I keep forgetting things. Just... basic adult things, really. Like paying bills, or following through on errands. And... well, I've been forgetting to return emails for interviews, or I just don't show up for appointments. It's... it's starting to cost me real opportunities. So... yeah. That's why I came in.
Have you struggled with this kind of forgetfulness and difficulty following through on tasks since you were a child, or is this a more recent change in your life?

Um... no, it's not new. It's... pretty much always been like this, I guess. 

Even back in elementary school, my teachers would write that I was bright, but... I don't know, I was constantly losing my worksheets. And... rushing through directions. They said I talked out of turn a lot, too. My desk was just... always so messy I could never find my assignments in it anyway. So... yeah. Since I was a kid.
Do you often feel like you are driven by a motor or have trouble sitting still for long periods of time?

Um... yeah, I guess so. I'm just... always doing something. Even without a job right now, I just kind of move from one thing to the next all day. Like... laundry, or emails, or... reorganizing browser tabs. Pacing. Starting dinner. 

It's like I just... can't really let myself stop. Even when... none of it actually gets finished.
Do you often find yourself interrupting others while they are talking or blurting out answers before a question is finished?

Um... yeah. I guess so. Like... in conversations, or even those interviews I mentioned. I just... I tend to jump in before the other person is done talking. 

I don't know, I always think I know where they're going with it, so I just... say it. But then... I realize I completely cut them off. Or... I end up answering the wrong question entirely. So... yeah. I do that.

Looking back at your life, would you say the difficulty with sitting still and the tendency to interrupt others has been just as much of a problem for you as the forgetfulness and trouble finishing tasks?
Um... yeah. I guess they've both always been there. It's hard to say if one is... worse than the other. They just kind of... happen together, I suppose.
